source.title: Implicit Convex Regularizers of CNN Architectures: Convex Optimization of Two- and Three-Layer Networks in Polynomial Time

record.tranche_reason: Reports CIFAR-10 and MNIST test accuracies for small three-layer circular CNN experiments, bearing on generalization after gradient training; its main contribution is an exact convex training formulation and implicit regularization characterization.
record.gate_note: The paper's theoretical equivalences and regularizer characterizations do not by themselves report generalization outcomes. Numerical experiments report training objectives and test accuracy for SGD-trained three-layer circular CNNs on a synthetic dataset and subsets of MNIST and CIFAR-10, plus an appendix comparison on full CIFAR-10. Figure-only accuracy results are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study characterizes convex formulations and regularizers of CNN training and compares optimization formulations. None of its results tests V1–V8. Reporting CNN test accuracy alone does not test any listed version; its width comparisons measure training-objective convergence, not generalization past interpolation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors derive exact finite-dimensional convex formulations for specified CNN architectures, establish polynomial training complexity under their stated conditions, and characterize architecture-dependent convex regularizers. Their numerical experiments illustrate optimization convergence and formulation-dependent test accuracy; they do not test V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use SGD on small three-layer circular CNNs and compare convex versus non-convex objectives; they do not use the original studies' random-label memorization, width, architecture-comparison, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or example-removal recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Filter count changes objective convergence on the synthetic example; the paper states all SGD trials converge to the convex optimum when filter count is large enough in the reported MNIST and CIFAR10 subset experiments. The CIFAR-10 appendix comparison varies the optimization objective.

fits_no_version.finding: In the reported CIFAR-10 binary-classification experiment, SGD optimization of the unconstrained convex formulation achieves a lower training objective and higher test accuracy than optimization of the conventional non-convex formulation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing the optimization formulation can improve held-out accuracy for the tested two-layer CNN.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing the synthetic circular CNN's filter count from five to fifteen changes convergence to the convex optimum from one of five SGD trials to all five trials.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing width can improve convergence to the optimal regularized training objective in the tested CNN.

record.problems: The numerical generalization evidence is limited to small subsets and binary classification in the main experiments, with accuracy presented in figures and no numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The appendix full CIFAR-10 accuracy comparison is also figure-only. No listed claim versions are directly tested.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately reported test-accuracy conditions are stated in text beyond the figure-only results captured. Figures 1, 2 and 4 contain plotted values that cannot be transcribed exactly from the supplied text.

untested.parts: No matched natural-label and random-label training and held-out comparisons.
No test-error comparison across widths beyond the zero-training-error threshold; synthetic width experiments measure regularized training objectives.
No convolutional versus fully connected held-out-performance comparison. Training-complexity arguments do not establish the claimed generalization advantage.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison or tuning intervention.
No batch-size comparison under a fixed epoch budget or adapted training recipe.
No dropout intervention or comparison involving joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking of generalization gaps.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification should be corrected. None of the listed versions receives a verdict. Missing exact figure values do not prevent this determination.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training, memorization-capacity comparison, or natural-label versus random-label test accuracy comparison.
No width sweep testing test error past the zero-training-error threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No large-batch comparison or batch-size sweep.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
No example removal or retraining comparison.
